scope: Actual parsed Verum source and independently decoded serialized VBC through production LLVM lowering and bounded host JIT. No fresh stdlib bake, ordinary CLI, AOT executable, allocator lifecycle, no-libc or registry acceptance.
findings: The initial native control process stopped with SIGSEGV on its first Int64 fixed-array consumer. Retained LLVM IR selects the exact Int64 source body and allocates eight packed bytes, but the caller reads generic container metadata from that raw buffer. This is incomplete execution and does not establish an owner-selection failure.

The bounded guard retains the same positive expectations and reports a failure before JIT when a packed-array fixture reaches generic container readers. Source and wire are attempted independently. USize/ISize List mutation through instance and alias/cast routes, and the scalar count_ones marker, pass on the isolated candidate.

The guarded baseline has five passing outer tests and three failing outer tests. The static test isolates all four competing declaration owners: its two List subcases pass, while its two fixed-array subcases remain red at the geometry guard.
controls: Every module contains competing USize/UInt64 and ISize/Int64 declarations. Descriptors retain AST-owned has_source_body through wire decode.
USize and ISize source methods return distinct growable Lists; UInt64 and Int64 source methods return distinct fixed packed arrays. Static, instance, cast and alias routes retain the declared owner.
The scalar USize.count_ones body returns a marker distinct from the primitive population count.
The adjacent native endian/storage suite runs unchanged on the combined source.
limitations: The host JIT allocator is a bounded fixture substrate, not runtime memory-management acceptance.

Early static subcases shared an IR filename in the guarded baseline, so its standalone static IR files contain only the final subcase; failed array IR remains verbatim in stderr. The follow-up test commit gives every owner a distinct IR filename for the integrated gate.
No bodyless-forward, borrowed numeric receiver, native AD, 128-bit, or native-endian acceptance is added by these eight owner tests.
